question: If 45º and 65º are the angles of a triangle, then find the exterior angle of the third angle (remaining angle).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the Exterior Angle Theorem, the exterior angle of a triangle is always equal to the sum of its two opposite (remote) interior angles.

The two given opposite interior angles are 45º and 65º.

Exterior angle of the third angle = 45º + 65º = 110º

**∴ The correct answer is 110º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two angles of a triangle are 45º and 65º.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all interior angles of a triangle = 180º

Interior angle + Exterior angle = 180º (Linear Pair)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the three interior angles of the triangle be ∠A, ∠B, and ∠C.

⇒ Let ∠A = 65º and ∠B = 45º

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180º

⇒ 65º + 45º + ∠C = 180º

⇒ 110º + ∠C = 180º

⇒ ∠C = 180º − 110º = 70º

⇒ The remaining third interior angle is 70º.

⇒ Exterior angle of ∠C = 180º − Interior ∠C (Linear Pair)

⇒ Exterior angle = 180º − 70º = 110º

**∴ The correct answer is 110º.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is always strictly equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote (opposite) interior angles.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles of a planar triangle is universally equal to 180º.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon (including a triangle), taking one at each vertex, is always 360º.
